nodes.content: Develop a semantic parser that distinguishes genuine utterance ambiguity from model uncertainty under unseen compositional structures.
requirements: Achieve ambiguity-detection F1 ≥0.85 on unseen compositions, using independently annotated sets of valid interpretations.
Match unambiguous-input execution accuracy of a single-output parser trained on identical data.

nodes.content: Keep a single-output execution backbone; flag ambiguity only when grammar-constrained, paraphrase-stable alternatives pass calibrated utterance–parse entailment.
What entailment and paraphrase-consistency thresholds reject beam-search artifacts without discarding valid alternative parses on unseen compositions?
Requiring entailment ≥0.80 and agreement across three of four paraphrases will yield ambiguity F1 ≥0.85 without reducing unambiguous execution accuracy.
Independently annotate valid-parse sets for unseen-composition CompoAmbig-1; sweep thresholds, comparing ambiguity F1 and unambiguous execution against the single-output baseline.
Sweep entailment and paraphrase thresholds around 0.80 and three-of-four on CompoAmbig-1; compare ambiguity F1 and unambiguous execution against single-output baseline.
On independently annotated CompoAmbig-1 unseen compositions, 0.80/three-of-four achieved ambiguity F1 0.87; unambiguous execution matched baseline at 91.2%.
Adopt 0.80 entailment and three-of-four paraphrase agreement: ambiguity F1 exceeds 0.85 while unambiguous execution matches baseline.
Freeze the adopted thresholds, then evaluate independently annotated CompoAmbig-2 unseen compositions and unambiguous execution against an identically trained single-output parser.
Run the frozen-threshold parser on independently annotated CompoAmbig-2; measure ambiguity F1 and unambiguous execution against the identically trained baseline.
CompoAmbig-2 evaluation bundle containing frozen-threshold predictions, independently annotated valid-parse sets, ambiguity F1, and paired unambiguous execution results.
Recompute CompoAmbig-2 bundle metrics from predictions and valid-parse sets; bootstrap F1 and execution gaps to check threshold compliance.
CompoAmbig-2 audit found ambiguity F1 0.86; unambiguous execution was 90.9% versus 90.9% for the identically trained single-output parser.
Operator-conditioned entailment thresholds will improve depth-four ambiguity precision by ≥3 points over fixed 0.80 without reducing valid-alternative recall.
Calibrate operator-specific thresholds on CompoAmbig-1; compare depth-four ambiguity precision and valid-alternative recall against fixed 0.80 on CompoAmbig-2.
On CompoAmbig-2 depth-four cases, operator thresholds raised ambiguity precision only 1.1 points; valid-alternative recall remained 89%.
Can paraphrase stability reject recurring parser errors when unseen operator nestings mislead both the backbone and entailment verifier?
Audit CompoAmbig-2 false ambiguity positives by operator nesting, testing whether three-of-four paraphrase agreement preserves shared backbone–verifier errors.
Retain the single-output backbone; use span-level scope charts and independently trained contrastive judgments to identify multiple licensed interpretations.
Train span-scope charts and a separate contrastive judge; evaluate CompoAmbig-3 ambiguity F1 and baseline-relative unambiguous execution.
Use the CompoAmbig-2 bundle to identify scope errors; train span-scope charts and a contrastive judge on shared-training-data hard negatives.
ScopeChart-v1 contains a span-scope generator and independently trained contrastive judge, leaving the single-output execution backbone unchanged.
Does ScopeChart-v1's contrastive judge reject spurious scope alternatives under unseen operator nestings while retaining valid alternatives?
On CompoAmbig-3 unseen nestings, ScopeChart-v1 will reject ≥80% of spurious scope alternatives while retaining ≥90% of annotated valid alternatives.
Run ScopeChart-v1 on independently annotated CompoAmbig-3 unseen nestings; measure spurious-alternative rejection, valid-alternative recall, ambiguity F1, and unambiguous execution.
On CompoAmbig-3, ScopeChart-v1 rejected 83% of spurious scope alternatives and retained 92% of annotated valid alternatives.
Keep ScopeChart-v1's contrastive scope filter for further evaluation: it rejects 83% of spurious alternatives while retaining 92% of valid alternatives.
Compare retained ScopeChart-v1 with the frozen-threshold parser on CompoAmbig-3: ambiguity F1, depth-four false positives, and baseline-relative unambiguous execution.
On CompoAmbig-3, frozen-threshold ambiguity F1 fell to 0.79 amid depth-four false positives; ScopeChart-v1 reached 0.87 with baseline-matched execution.
CompoAmbig-3 depth-four false positives will disproportionately reflect shared backbone–verifier scope errors that survive three-of-four paraphrase agreement.
Use ScopeChart-v1 and annotated parses to compare shared backbone–verifier errors among depth-four versus shallower three-of-four-agreement false positives.
Among paraphrase-stable false positives, shared scope errors occurred in 68% of depth-four cases versus 24% shallower; ScopeChart-v1 rejected 79%.
Can ScopeChart-v1 distinguish genuinely ambiguous scope readings from missing gold interpretations when independent annotators disagree on CompoAmbig-3?
Blinded adjudication will validate ≥75% of ScopeChart-v1’s unlisted readings on disputed items, versus ≤15% on unanimously unambiguous items.
Blindly adjudicate ScopeChart-v1 unlisted readings on CompoAmbig-3 disputed and unanimously unambiguous items, stratified by audited depth-four scope errors.
Blinded adjudication validated 78% of disputed versus 12% of unanimous unlisted readings; missed interpretations lowered corrected CompoAmbig-3 F1 to 0.83.
Retain ScopeChart-v1’s scope filter but defer deployment; adjudicate missing readings and retune because corrected ambiguity F1 is 0.83.
Train ScopeChart-v2 on adjudicated valid-parse sets; use calibrated scope-coverage confidence to separate uncertain parses from corroborated alternatives, preserving execution.
Which scope-coverage confidence cutoff separates corroborated alternatives from incomplete charts on unseen nestings without suppressing adjudicated valid readings?
Scope-coverage ≥0.75 will yield ambiguity F1 ≥0.85 and valid-alternative recall ≥90% on adjudicated CompoAmbig-4 unseen nestings.
Adjudicate missing readings, retrain ScopeChart-v2, tune coverage cutoff on CompoAmbig-3, then test CompoAmbig-4 F1, recall, and execution.
Extend ScopeChart-v1 with adjudicated valid readings; retrain ScopeChart-v2 and calibrate coverage cutoff on held-out CompoAmbig-3 items.
ScopeChart-v2 revises v1 with adjudication-trained scope judgments and calibrated coverage gating, retaining the unchanged single-output execution backbone.
Evaluate ScopeChart-v2 at 0.75 coverage on independently adjudicated CompoAmbig-4; measure ambiguity F1, valid-alternative recall, and baseline-relative unambiguous execution.
On adjudicated CompoAmbig-4, ScopeChart-v2 achieved ambiguity F1 0.87, valid-alternative recall 92%, and unambiguous execution 91.0%, matching baseline.
Does ScopeChart-v2’s coverage gate mistake shared scope errors for genuine ambiguity when entire operator families are withheld during training?
On adjudicated CompoAmbig-5 withheld-operator families, ≥20% of coverage-accepted ambiguity flags will reflect shared scope errors.
Create adjudicated CompoAmbig-5 operator-family holdouts; audit accepted ambiguity flags for shared scope errors and compare F1 against CompoAmbig-4.
Run ScopeChart-v2 on adjudicated CompoAmbig-5 withheld families; manually classify coverage-accepted flags and compute shared-error rate and ambiguity F1.
On adjudicated CompoAmbig-5, 26% of coverage-accepted ambiguity flags were shared scope errors; ambiguity F1 fell to 0.81.
Retain ScopeChart-v2 for tested compositions, but defer withheld-operator deployment: ambiguity F1 was 0.87 on CompoAmbig-4 versus 0.81 on CompoAmbig-5.
Add symbolic operator-scope checks to ScopeChart-v2; evaluate adjudicated CompoAmbig-6 family holdouts for ambiguity F1 ≥0.85 and baseline-matched execution.
Implement ScopeChart-v3 by adding symbolic operator-scope checks to v2’s ambiguity branch, leaving its single-output execution backbone unchanged.
ScopeChart-v3 revises v2 with symbolic operator-scope validation before ambiguity flags; its single-output execution backbone remains unchanged.
Evaluate ScopeChart-v3 on adjudicated CompoAmbig-6 withheld-operator families; measure ambiguity F1, shared-scope false positives, and baseline-relative unambiguous execution.
On adjudicated CompoAmbig-6 family holdouts, ScopeChart-v3 reached ambiguity F1 0.86; shared-scope errors affected 11% of flags, execution matched baseline.
Advance ScopeChart-v3 for further testing: v2 passed CompoAmbig-4 but failed family holdouts, whereas v3 met both requirements.
